ThingDef.label: Helghan Assault Armor
ThingDef.description: In many ways the foundational infantry kit of the entire army, the assault loadout forgoes the trench coat for unrestrictive gear optimized for tight urban fights. Whilst technically unimpressive, the assault kit is a conservative idea built on centuries of human combat experience. Replaceable armor plates created to dampen rifle caliber rounds to the chest, whilst the tox-resistant uniform mesh is worn overtop of the body, fitted to prevent slowdown via series of small straps. The outfit is warm to wear, but not so much that it is unusable in arid warmer climates. Every suit bears an integrated replaceable air recycler unit, and a supply of fast acting sealant to patch up suit damage. Nevertheless, in the face of armor piercing rounds, well aimed shots, and charge weaponry, this gear falls short. Perhaps its greatest achievement is simply in being slightly more maneuverable than regular flak gear. Propaganda insists the fibers are flame retardant, but evidence from the frontline suggests otherwise.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather Assault Armor
ThingDef.description: This version of the common assault armor has been weather proofed for the harsh climes associated with remote research installations or corporate facilities favored by Helghan Corporation. Troops like this formed large reserve units which survived the battle of Pyrrhus and reorganized briefly under Stahl and Orlock during the final weeks of Helghan. Tactically, there is very little different between this and conventional assault armor, outside its warm fur lined interior to enable operations in harsh arctic environments with some Helghan wartime plans caling for evacuating into the frozen steppe to wage a war of attrition in conditions no normal human could withstand for long making heavy use of this cold weather gear.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Rifleman Trench-kit
ThingDef.description: Originally seen as a reservist outfit, the 'Trench-kit' - so named for the riflemen oft expected to hold static positions and its notable trench-coat, performs roughly the same as the assault kit, with the benefit of being more comfortable in cold conditions. Sometimes used as a poor mans stand-in for proper cold weather gear, this outfits reputation changed during the invasion of the Helghan home world, where it became far more prevalent among rapidly trained or conscripted infantry detachments. Despite technically being slightly better protection than typical assault standard issue, owing to the thick trench coat, the Helghan Empire typically only produces this gear in times of great need. For distant outposts in the far north or south, this gear can be considered lifesaving. Of course, it retains all its tox resistant properties it had with the assault load.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather Patrol Armor
ThingDef.description: A common sight in remote Helghan corporate research outposts or detention facilities, Patrol Armor like this was made to survey long perimeters in cold, irradiated conditions. Troops assigned to these details pack extra survival equipment, as accidents or enemy action may keep them away from logistics lines for days at a time. To help find bodies in the snow, bright decals showing unit or corporate affiliation clash against the otherwise stark white camoflage.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Grenadier Flak Kit
ThingDef.description: Heavy, cumbersome, and a poor substitute for real EOD gear, the grenadiers at times loathe their unwieldy suits, woven with thick fibers to imbue the kit with blast and shrapnel resistant qualities. The Helghan regime stopped short of substantially improving the armors performance, leaving many grenadiers to feel exposed and awkward compared to their nimble counterparts. They maintain distance, using medium to long range grenade launchers to back up nearby forces. In a pinch, they can sometimes be called upon to use heavy squad support weaponry, but this is rare. Grenadiers were envisioned as part of heavy helghan mechanized infantry regiments, deploying from IFV's and personnel carriers amidst an enemy position, but since the loss of much of helghan's armored division, these troopers were forced to march with their lesser cousins. They enjoy better armor than most of their colleagues, but are a far cry from the upper echelon of the helghan army.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather Tank Hunter Armor
ThingDef.description: Helghan tank hunters were originally intended as detached company level specialist teams, to set up ambushes in defensive positions to pick off isolated armored units. It was assumed the Helghan armored divisions would handle most of the heavy lifting in defeating the ISAs vehicles, This proved not to be the case during the siege of Pyrrhus, and so under Radec's direction, Tank hunters teams were reorganized and greatly expanded. This stratagem was adopted by the wider army, and today most successor states consider anti tank troops or 'rockers' as they and the ISA have taken to calling them, as organic squad level assets. A result of this has been the rise in rocket troops gleefully deploying their anti tank weaponry against infantry targets. Rather than trying to curtail the behavior, the army has instead attempted to keep up with the ammuntion demands of its bloodthirsty troops.\n\nThis armor has been cold-weather proofed, and adorned with winter fatigues. The inside has been lined and padded to better retain heat, and the normally exposed areas have been sealed up for long term exposure to the elements.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Advanced Shock BDU
ThingDef.description: This armor represents a cut above the standard line trooper's gear, with a bulletproof kevlar plated vest worn overtop of typical shock trooper kit + an advanced rebreather unit for better performance in toxic environments. This outfit was not unique to one particular army unit - not even its namesake 'advanced shock troopers', but rather it was worn by a wide variety of Helghan regulars who were trusted with the latest army-issue hardware. This equipment is utilized by company level machine-gun operators, commando elements, veteran riflemen, certain tank crews, and many more. During the war for the Helghan, these uniforms would be equipped the same day they were assembled. Now, their popularity has waned somewhat; better more advanced armor systems often replace this equipment in modern splinter states of Helghan.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather Assault Hardsuit
ThingDef.description: Seen as a sort of half-measure between the Shock Army's experimental powered armor projects and later generation full body suits, the Hardsuit was an attempt at upgrading regular infantry gear, exchanging movement speed for survivability. On the surface, it appears to be conventional infantry gear with an armor plate covering the upper chest, However, below the outer layers it has layered pads inserted at the pelvis, thighs, and stomach area to prevent mortal wounds. The metal plate was intended to cover the exposed parts of an infantryman peeking from cover, so these suits naturally lent themselves to defensive tactics, and became fairly common in helghan fire support units. As an interim armor phase, they were somewhat unpopular, and the high weight clashed with Helghan doctrine, leading to their gradual phase out in successor regimes. Still, these did not cost advanced components to create, making them attractive for helghan garrisons in trench warfare postures that needed heavy armor for cheap.\n\nThis Hardsuit has been cold-weather proofed, and adorned with winter fatigues. The inside has been lined and padded to better retain heat, and the normally exposed areas have been sealed up for long term exposure to the elements.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Scout BDU
ThingDef.description: Helghast scouts served as the primary ISR wing of the Helghan ground forces, attempting to conduct recon-in-force operations to identify targets for artillery and air strikes. A subgroup of Helghan light infantry, scout units were intended to be highly mobile units, and so while infiltration was a focus of training, mobility and skirmish tactics were the main focuses for these soldiers. During the war, scout formations regularly became candidates for sniper school thanks to a large number of transferrable skills, and soon Helghan marksmen and scouts became mostly interchangeable terms, as the regime began prioritizing the usage of snipers to whittle down ISA forces. Contrary to myth, the sniper armor itself is a fairly simple affair; a weather treated poncho/smock worn overtop standard Helghan BDU's. The smock allegedly assists with protection from fragmentation shrapnel thanks to its material composition, but most rightly dismiss this claim as regime propaganda. Snipers prefer to 'shoot and scoot' to avoid learning the hard way what most guess: their personal protection is some of the weakest in the army.\n\nInfamous among ISA infantry formations, this expensive optic headset became associated with excellent marksmanship. Onboard HUD and advanced rangefinder software link in with weapon profiles for most Helghan and ISA sniper rifles, guiding users shots, greatly cutting down on aim-time and enhancing accuracy. Of course, this sort of excellence doesn't come without costs: the computer systems within the goggles make them heavy, which is not a problem as most users forgo helmets when wearing these, instead using a thermal cover underneath their concealing hood to allow for comfort in extreme weather conditions. It goes without saying it does very little to keep its user alive when the foe begins to return fire.
